answer: One concrete mechanism: a new identity must burn a bounded amount of compute, roughly one CPU-hour of hash work, before it can earn anything, and every submission stakes part of its balance that reputation-weighted juries can slash. The beacon words fit the design: ivory maps onto the cold reserve that unlocks only after honest work, mirror captures the flow of attestations that gives each answer finality, and sable mirrors the compute burned to admit each new identity. An attacker minting N fake identities pays N times that burn up front, then loses each stake a jury rejects.
